content.text: {"quote_faithful":"yes","verdict":"confirmed","evidence_kind":"invalid_inference","fatal":"yes","explanation":"Claim 3.2 quantifies over every inclusion-minimal transversal T, but π(T) is defined only for finite T. No prior argument makes such a T finite. Indeed, even an intersecting family of finite sets can have an infinite minimal transversal: for C={{c,x_n}: n≥1}, the set {x_n:n≥1} is inclusion-minimal and infinite. Thus the displayed inference to π(T)∈S∞ is unjustified for the T obtained inside I∪Z_ω. Step 4 then uses self-duality to conclude that this T belongs to C and hence is finite; that is precisely the unsupported implication. Since this conclusion is needed to place T inside some finite I∪Z_s and obtain the final antichain contradiction, the finiteness argument—and therefore the lower_bound obligation—remains incomplete."}
